title: Agent Archivist catalog rebuild result (archivist.cli-result/v1)
description: The result document of the `catalog rebuild --from-occurrences` command (plan Phase 10; CLI-015): the cumulative state one deterministic rebuild fold reached over the tenant's frozen raw prefix — the pipeline and projection identity the derivation ran under, the frozen inventory digest, the occurrence and attestation totals, the four usage-row coverage states, and the checkpoint chain's terminal digests and key. Every member is cumulative rebuild state, not run state: a one-shot and a resumed rebuild of one raw prefix emit the same document bytes, which is why the document carries no timestamp — the wall-clock lives in the CLI output envelope's `generated_at` member (CLI-014), never in the rebuild's own state. Every figure is a content-free counter, a digest of already-stored bytes, or a closed-vocabulary identifier; no member carries a transcript body, a raw object path, a secret value or reference string, or a monetary amount (SEC-004).

x-archivist.compatibility: member additions are additive within v1 per plan Section 7.1 (CLI-015); redefining or removing a member, or a new namespace, is a v2 event

schema.description: The CLI result namespace. Present in every result document so a consumer always knows which contract it is reading before anything else (VAL-001); an unknown namespace is not this format and fails closed.

catalog_rebuild_version.description: The rebuild checkpoint document's own schema major (plan Section 7.10): the version of the checkpoint state the fold emits and resumes through, independent of the pipeline axis below. Integer, currently 1.

pipeline_id.description: The derived pipeline whose fold produced this state (plan Section 7.1 derived-pipeline axis). v1 ships exactly one, the deterministic `usage` projection of the catalog rebuild; a future producer reports its own id and writes under its own derived prefix segment — never by repurposing `usage`'s. Security-bearing: the pipeline names the trust the chain digest rests on, so an unknown value fails closed.

pipeline_version.description: The immutable version of that pipeline's mapping (v1 pins `1`): the rules that turn raw usage bytes into coverage states are frozen inside a version, and a changed mapping is a new version, never a silent rewrite of an old chain (plan Section 7.1: rebuildable).

usage_summary_version.description: The usage-summary record-shape major the fold emits (plan Section 7.10): the version axis of the rows the rebuild counted, independent of the pipeline axis. Integer, currently 1.

usage_projection_version.description: The immutable version of the adapter projection whose usage reader the fold ran (plan Section 7.1; STO-010). This member makes the counts reproducible: the same raw prefix read by a different projection version is a different derivation, a different chain digest, and a different checkpoint — never a silent reinterpretation of an old state.

tenant_id.description: The one tenant whose raw prefix the rebuild folded (plan Section 7.5). The rebuild is tenant-scoped like every derived path: the catalog and derived namespaces it writes are this tenant's, and the checkpoint key below is inside the same scope.

inventory_digest.description: The digest of the frozen inventory-v1 enumeration the fold ran over (plan Section 7.10): the identity of the exact raw prefix the state covers. The chain's genesis binds this digest, so a chain can never be replayed against a different prefix.

occurrences_total.description: The occurrences in the frozen prefix this rebuild covers — the cumulative denominator the fold enumerated, whether it reached them in one pass or through resumed passes.

attestations_observed.description: The upload attestations the fold observed across the covered prefix — the commit-boundary evidence the fold read, counted separately from the occurrences it names.

row_states.description: The four usage-row coverage states the fold tallied (plan Phase 10): measured, absent, malformed, and unsupported — always all four, because a zero is an observation here, not an absence, and an incomplete source can never read as free.

chain_digest.description: The checkpoint chain's terminal digest: the cumulative fold's self-verifying commitment, each checkpoint framing the one before it, so two rebuilds of one raw prefix and pipeline version converge on the same chain and a divergent one is detectable (plan Phase 10 exit gate).

checkpoint_digest.description: The terminal checkpoint document's own SHA-256 — the content address the checkpoint is written under, so the state a consumer resumes from is verified against its own key before any of it is trusted (VAL-005).

checkpoint_key.description: The derived catalog-checkpoint key the terminal state is stored at, inside the tenant's `catalog/` namespace: the resume pointer a later pass lists and re-verifies. The key carries the tenant identifier and the checkpoint's own digest and nothing else — no bucket, no endpoint, no credential material.

complete.description: Whether the fold covered the frozen inventory to exhaustion: false is the bounded honest state of a pass that stopped inside the policy's window — the resume pointer above is where the next pass continues, never a silent partial read (plan Section 7.10).

measured.description: Rows whose usage the pinned projection read from the raw bytes.

absent.description: Rows whose source carried no usage at all — the bounded `unknown` state, never zero, so an incomplete source can never read as free (plan Phase 10).

malformed.description: Rows whose source usage was present but unusable — shapes the pinned reader refuses.

unsupported.description: Rows whose source usage the pinned projection version does not support — a future reader version may, and then this denominator moves under a new projection version, never inside this one.

row-states.description: The four usage-row coverage states, all required: the rebuild reports what it measured and, with equal precision, what it could not.
